newsitem.title: FRANCE: French ex-tycoon Bernard Tapie gets new jail term.
newsitem.headline: French ex-tycoon Bernard Tapie gets new jail term.

text.p: A French court on Friday sentenced imprisoned bankrupt tycoon Bernard Tapie to an additional 18 months in jail with another 18 months suspended for embezzling funds from Marseille soccer club.
Tapie attorney Jean-Yves Lienard quickly announced he would appeal, calling the sentence "totally out of proportion" to his client's alleged crime.
During Tapie's trial in May, a public prosecutor had urged the court in the Mediterranean port city of Marseille to jail the former soccer boss for two years, with another two years suspended.
The 54-year-old businessman and former political boss was charged with embezzling 100 million francs ($17.5 million) between 1987 and 1993 when he was president of the Marseille club.
All 19 of Tapie's co-defendants, who held various club posts or were otherwise involved in French soccer, were also convicted in the case and drew fines or jail terms.
The trial failed to determine where the embezzled funds ended up but highlighted widespread illegal practices in soccer including false invoicing and kickbacks.
During the trial, Tapie admitted breaking the law with fictitious loans to star players but argued that what he had done was less illicit than other possible courses of action.
He also admitted using gate money to bribe rival players to lose a 1993 match.
The proceedings were repeatedly suspended for medical treatment when the former political boss and leftist cabinet minister began suffering chest pains and breathing difficulties.
At the close of the trial, Tapie had pleaded with the judge not to sentence him to additional jail time.

"I was a great star. For the past three years I have suffered everything, I have been ruined, dishonoured, humiliated. And you are asked to insist on the only thing left to me: the possibility of being in touch with my family," the former cabinet minister Tapie told the court.
But the public prosecutor countered that Tapie had "no regard for the morality of sport".

Tapie was imprisoned earlier this year after the supreme court upheld an eight-month sentence for bribing players of league rival Valenciennes to give Marseille an easy game, days before Marseille beat AC Milan in the 1993 European Cup final.
The Marseille court rejected a bid by Tapie that he be allowed to serve the two sentences concurrently.

Among the other defendants, Alain Laroche, the club's former finance director, was convicted and sentenced to six months in jail with another 18 months suspended, while Jean-Pierre Bernes, Tapie's former right-hand man on the team, was given a 30-month suspended sentence.
Bernes had described the "loans" to star players as compensation, testifying that in this way the Marseille club did not have to pay payroll taxes on the sums.
Former Marseille sporting director and French national soccer coach Michel Hidalgo was given a one-year suspended sentence. He had testified that he approved the loans on management orders.
Club controller Elie Fellous was given a six-month prison term with another 18 months suspended.

Greek agent Spiridon Karegeorgis, tried in his absence, was sentenced to 18 months in prison while former Croatian agent Ljubomir Barin, who had been extradited from Germany to stand trial, was given a six-month suspended sentence.
Portuguese sports intermediary Miguel Barbosa drew a year's suspended sentence.
